title: Functions, Scope & Modern ES6+
description: Master JavaScript functions in all their forms — declarations, expressions, arrow functions, closures, and higher-order functions. Add modern ES6+ features like destructuring, spread, rest, and modules to your toolkit.
learningObjectives: Write functions using declarations, expressions, and arrow syntax
Understand scope: global, function, block, and lexical
Explain closures and why they matter
Use destructuring, spread, rest, and optional chaining
Import and export with ES6 modules

sections.content: Three Ways to Write a Function

exercises.question: What does an arrow function return when used without curly braces? e.g., const double = x => x * 2
options: undefined
The expression value (implicit return)
An error
null
hints: No curly braces = concise body = implicit return
exercises.explanation: Arrow functions without curly braces use an implicit return — the expression result is automatically returned. With curly braces, you must use explicit return.

sections.content: A closure is a function that remembers the variables from its outer scope even after that outer function has finished executing. This is one of JavaScript's most powerful and commonly-used features.

exercises.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A way to close a browser window
A function that has access to its outer scope's variables even after the outer function returns
A method to end a loop early
A private class variable
exercises.correctAnswer: A function that has access to its outer scope's variables even after the outer function returns
hints: The inner function 'closes over' the outer variables
exercises.explanation: A closure is formed when an inner function retains access to its outer function's variables after the outer function has completed. This enables patterns like private state, factory functions, and memoization.

exercises.question: What does the ?. (optional chaining) operator do?
options: It makes properties optional in TypeScript
It returns undefined instead of throwing if the object is null/undefined
It checks if a value is defined before assigning
It is the same as && for null checks
exercises.correctAnswer: It returns undefined instead of throwing if the object is null/undefined
exercises.explanation: user?.address?.city returns undefined if user or address is null/undefined, instead of throwing a TypeError. It short-circuits the whole chain as soon as a null/undefined is encountered.

sections.content: In JavaScript, functions are values — they can be assigned to variables, passed as arguments, and returned from other functions. A higher-order function either takes a function as an argument or returns one.

exercises.question: Which correctly defines a higher-order function?
options: A function defined inside a class
A function that only uses const variables
A function that accepts a function as argument or returns a function
A function called more than once
exercises.correctAnswer: A function that accepts a function as argument or returns a function
exercises.explanation: A higher-order function treats functions as values — either by accepting them as parameters (like Array.map(callback)) or returning new functions (like factory functions and currying).

exercises.question: How many default exports can a single ES6 module file have?
options: Unlimited
Two
One
Zero
hints: 'default' implies there is only one of them
exercises.explanation: Each module can have only one default export, but unlimited named exports. Named exports are imported with { } and must match the export name (unless aliased with 'as').

capstoneProject.title: Utility Library
capstoneProject.description: Build a modular JavaScript utility library with functions organized across multiple ES6 module files.
requirements: array.js: chunk(), flatten(), unique(), groupBy() utility functions
Each function is a named export
index.js re-exports all functions from one entry point
All functions use closures or higher-order patterns where appropriate
Test each function in a demo.js file using dynamic imports
